# The command line

<!-- purpose: Every `swcraft` command and option, and what each option does when left out -->

*This page is generated from SWCraft's own definitions, and describes the version you have installed.*

Everything SWCraft does to a project is one `swcraft` command. Most of them are pointed at a project with `--project` and the path to its `swcraft.yaml`; every one of them is listed below with each option it accepts, what that option takes and what it does when you leave it out.

`swcraft agent` hands everything written after it to the assistant, whose own commands and options are declared by another program and are not listed here; the page about the assistant covers them.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`swcraft init`](#swcraft-init) | Scaffold a new SWCraft project directory |
| [`swcraft generate`](#swcraft-generate) | Generate output files from the YAML model |
| [`swcraft validate`](#swcraft-validate) | Validate the model, generate the ARXML and check it against the AUTOSAR XSD (structurally, saying so, when no licensed XSD is configured) |
| [`swcraft check-model`](#swcraft-check-model) | Validate the model only (no artifact generation; build-graph-safe) |
| [`swcraft diff`](#swcraft-diff) | Semantic diff between two model revisions (git-diff-like arg semantics) |
| [`swcraft impact`](#swcraft-impact) | Transitive dependents of one named element (always the working tree) |
| [`swcraft list`](#swcraft-list) | List every declared layer's elements by identity (read-only; always exits 0 on a successful run) |
| [`swcraft query`](#swcraft-query) | Filtered, member-sliced and paged slices of one layer, or one bounded walk (read-only; a project it cannot read and a request it cannot answer both exit 1) |
| [`swcraft resource-report`](#swcraft-resource-report) | Print the resource utilization report (read-only without --report; always exits 0 — 'swcraft validate' is the gate) |
| [`swcraft mcp-serve`](#swcraft-mcp-serve) | Launch the swcraft MCP server |
| [`swcraft agent`](#swcraft-agent) | Talk to the assistant about this project (everything written after 'agent' is its own command line) |
| [`swcraft clean-outputs`](#swcraft-clean-outputs) | Remove the two directories this project generates into, so a failing build leaves nothing stale behind |
| [`swcraft import`](#swcraft-import) | Import an external architecture export into a SWCraft project (model: bulk into a fresh project; component: safe merge into an existing one; requirements: one requirements interchange file into an existing one) |
| [`swcraft docs`](#swcraft-docs) | Open the SWCraft user guide that came with this install, served on this machine |
| [`swcraft experiment`](#swcraft-experiment) | Run an experiment of one kind: 'allocation' (where can a component move, and what does it buy) or 'trace' (which elements may a requirement be linked to); a search writes a report and nothing into the model, and 'trace --apply' writes the decided links into it |
| [`swcraft guard`](#swcraft-guard) | Answer an agent host's PreToolUse hook: read the tool call's JSON payload on stdin and answer in the host's form -- for Copilot, Codex and Claude Code the decision printed on stdout, exit 0; for Kiro a denial is exit 2 with one line on stderr and an allow exit 0 with nothing printed. For Copilot (the default), deny a known file tool's read or search that reaches the model directory or cannot be judged; for Codex (--host codex), also deny a patch or a shell command that reaches it; for Claude Code (--host claude), also deny an edit, a write or a shell command that reaches it, and every PowerShell call; for Kiro (--host kiro), judge Kiro's read, search, edit and shell tools alike and deny every tool it does not know; allow the rest (changes nothing) |
| [`swcraft change-report`](#swcraft-change-report) | Report what a change does to the architecture -- what changed, requirement links, the findings it introduced, resources, interface consumers, ARXML elements and the overviews before and after -- into &lt;dist_root>/change-report/ (git-diff-like revision arguments; writes nothing into the model) |
| [`swcraft passport`](#swcraft-passport) | Write the model's passport -- counts, distributions and lengths, with no name, no value and no text of the model -- as JSON to stdout or to --output, to send instead of a model that cannot be shared (writes nothing into the model) |
| [`swcraft metrics`](#swcraft-metrics) | Print the architecture metrics -- size, coupling, cohesion, coverage and integrity, each explained, and how they moved since a revision (read-only without --report; always exits 0 -- 'swcraft validate' is the gate) |

## `swcraft init` { #swcraft-init }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft init`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Scaffold a new SWCraft project directory

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `PATH` | one value | required | Target directory to initialise |
| `--name` | `NAME` | — | Project name (default: the target directory name) |
| `--integration` | one of `moon` | — | Also scaffold a build integration: 'moon' writes the vehicle-architecture template (moon build graph, the toolchain version pin, the chosen chat clients' files) |
| `--client` | one of `copilot`, `codex`, `claude`, `kiro` | — | With --integration moon: a chat client to set the project up for, repeatable: 'copilot' for GitHub Copilot, 'codex' for Codex (OpenAI), 'claude' for Claude Code (Anthropic), 'kiro' for Kiro; default: copilot. Needs --integration moon |

## `swcraft generate` { #swcraft-generate }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft generate`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Generate output files from the YAML model

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |

## `swcraft query` { #swcraft-query }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft query`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Filtered, member-sliced and paged slices of one layer, or one bounded walk (read-only; a project it cannot read and a request it cannot answer both exit 1)

This command writes no file. It always succeeds on a run that could read the project and answer the request — an empty answer is still an answer. It reports two failures: a project it could not read, and a request it refuses — one the model's declarations cannot answer (a filter naming an undeclared field, `--members` naming no declared collection, an `--after` cursor the slice does not carry, a `--request` naming no declared layer, a computed value it names that none is or that is computed at another set, a filter over a computed value it does not ask for or naming no value of it, a filter asking a set-valued computed value for no value, which yields no row to find, or a join path that names no value of the row it reads), or one the arguments themselves refuse (a `--limit` or a `--depth` below 1, an unreadable or malformed `--request` file, and the combinations that mix the layer slice, the walk and `--request`).

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `LAYER` | one of `requirements`, `compositions`, `swc`, `interfaces`, `application_types`, `implementation_types`, `base_types`, `units`, `compu_methods`, `data_constraints`, `mapping_sets`, `connectors`, `tasks`, `sequences`, `hardware` | — | The layer to slice (omit it and give --dependents or --deps NAME to walk the reference graph) |
| `--dependents` | `NAME` | — | Walk to the elements that depend on NAME (grouped by the matched element's layer, named by its singular token — `interface`, not the `interfaces` a LAYER slice takes) |
| `--deps` | `NAME` | — | Walk to the elements NAME depends on (the same walk, the same layer tokens, the other direction) |
| `--where` | `FIELD=VALUE`, repeatable | — | Keep the elements whose declared FIELD equals VALUE (repeatable; the clauses are AND-composed) |
| `--exists` | `FIELD`, repeatable | — | Keep the elements that carry a value for the declared FIELD; null and the empty string are no value (repeatable; AND-composed) |
| `--members` | `FIELD` | — | Answer every member of the declared collection FIELD across the layer, beside its owner; a dotted path of collections (runnables.writes) also names the members it passes through |
| `--form` | one of `index`, `full` | — | How wide each row is: `index` (the identity; the default) or `full` (every declared field, as the MCP `read` answers at `full`) |
| `--limit` | `N` | — | Answer at most N rows, with the total and a cursor to continue past (LAYER slices only) |
| `--after` | `ID` | — | Continue past the identity ID, which a previous page answered as its cursor (needs --limit) |
| `--request` | `FILE` | — | Read the whole request from FILE, a JSON object with the keys of the MCP read request minus `operation` (its address names a layer); given alone, beside no LAYER, slice or walk argument. A `where` clause may name `derived.NAME.PATH`, a value of a computed value the request asks for in `derived`; asking a set-valued one for no value (`exists: false`, `equals: null`) is refused |
| `--depth` | `N` | — | Bound a walk to N levels (default: the whole transitive walk; walks only) |
| `--project` | `PATH` | — | Path to swcraft.yaml manifest (required) |
| `--format` | one of `text`, `json` | `text` | Output format: 'text' (default, one 'layer: identity' line, at --form full followed by one indented 'field: value' line per field) or 'json' (versioned, machine-readable) |

`--dependents` and `--deps` cannot be given together.

## `swcraft resource-report` { #swcraft-resource-report }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft resource-report`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Print the resource utilization report (read-only without --report; always exits 0 — 'swcraft validate' is the gate)

Without `--report` this command writes no file. With it, it also writes `<dist_root>/resource-report/resource-report.md`, nothing into the model, and prints where. A report that cannot be written is a warning and moves no exit code; a project pinned to another SWCraft release gets its answer and a warning, and no file. It always succeeds on a run that could read the project — an empty or an uncomfortable answer is still an answer. A project it could not read is the failure it reports.

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `--project` | `PATH` | — | Path to swcraft.yaml manifest (required) |
| `--format` | one of `text`, `json` | `text` | Output format: 'text' (default) or 'json' (versioned, machine-readable) |
| `--fit-bytes` | `N` | — | Ask whether N more bytes fit each memory, within its threshold and within its size |
| `--fit-utilization` | `U` | — | Ask whether a share U of a core (0.05 or 1/20) fits each core, within its threshold and the whole core |
| `--report` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | Also write the report as Markdown to &lt;dist_root>/resource-report/resource-report.md |

`--fit-bytes` and `--fit-utilization` cannot be given together.

## `swcraft import` { #swcraft-import }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft import`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Import an external architecture export into a SWCraft project (model: bulk into a fresh project; component: safe merge into an existing one; requirements: one requirements interchange file into an existing one)

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `FORMAT` | one of `model`, `component`, `requirements` | required | Source format: 'model' (whole-export bulk import, fresh project only), 'component' (one component-scoped ARXML export, existing project) or 'requirements' (one requirements interchange file, existing project) |
| `--source` | `FILE` | — | Path to the ARXML export file, or for 'requirements' the requirements interchange file (required) |
| `--project` | `PATH` | — | Path to swcraft.yaml manifest of the target project (required; must be fresh for 'model', may be non-empty for 'component' and 'requirements') |
| `--packages` | `P1,P2,...` | — | model only: comma-separated package selection (dependency closure applied automatically); default imports the whole export |
| `--report` | `PATH` | — | Also write the human-readable import report to this file (model, component and requirements alike); for component and requirements a PATH ending in .md gets the report as Markdown, any other PATH the text printed; model always writes the text |
| `--dry-run` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | Compute and print the report without writing any files (model, component and requirements alike) |
| `--force` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | model only: allow importing into a non-empty project model (no merge protection) |
| `--verbose` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | model only: list every skipped element under its reason; by default the report prints one line per reason with its count |
| `--update` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | component only: explicitly replace the target's own divergent definition of the imported SWC (only that one file; a semantic diff preview is included in the report). Never affects a divergent shared interface/data type — that always aborts. Without it, an import whose only conflict is that divergent component exits with status 3 instead of 1, so a script can tell the refusal this option resolves from every other. |
| `--replace-access-lists` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | component only, with --update: also take the source export's runnable read/write/call lists, even though the export does not say whether it can express them. Without this the component's existing lists are kept and the report says so. |
| `--mapping` | `FILE` | — | requirements only: a YAML file mapping the requirements team's need types and field names to SWCraft's; it must lie outside the model directory. Without it, SWCraft's own names apply |
| `--baseline` | `TEXT` | — | requirements only: the version of this requirements delivery (the team's baseline or commit), recorded on every requirement it holds; it wins over the file's own version. Without it, the file's version is used, and a file with none is refused |

## `swcraft experiment` { #swcraft-experiment }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft experiment`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Run an experiment of one kind: 'allocation' (where can a component move, and what does it buy) or 'trace' (which elements may a requirement be linked to); a search writes a report and nothing into the model, and 'trace --apply' writes the decided links into it

This command writes its report under `<dist_root>/experiments/<name>/`, or into the directory its configuration's `output` names inside the project: `report.md` and `result.json`, and for `trace` also `proposals.json`, which each run rewrites whole. A search writes nothing into the model; `trace --apply FILE` is the one form that does: it writes the links decided in that proposals file into the model, records the decisions in `trace-decisions.yaml`, marks them done in the file, all or nothing, and with `--dry-run` writes nothing; `trace --documents` writes nothing either: it prints each document's requirements and links and the pass the configuration gives it. It succeeds on a run that could read the project and answer the experiment: for `allocation`, no improvement at any number of moves and no component free to move are still answers; for `trace`, no requirement in scope and a requirement with no candidate are, and for `--apply`, nothing to do and every decision stale. It reports the failures it has, and writes nothing on any of them: a flag given to a form it does not apply to, a project it could not read, a configuration file or a name in it that it refuses, a report directory outside the project, over the model or on a file, a configured one inside `.git` or already holding a report another tool or person wrote, and a project pinned to another SWCraft release; for `allocation` also a model `check-model` refuses (a warning is not a refusal, and `--warnings-as-errors` is `check-model`'s flag, not this command's), the solver absent, an experiment the solver's integers cannot represent and a solver that fails to run the experiment; for a `trace` search also a model in which a name an element's address or a requirement id is built from is declared twice, a malformed or unreadable `trace-decisions.yaml`, and a previous proposals file holding decisions not yet applied, one it cannot read as a proposals file or one changed while the search ran, unless `--discard-pending` is given, while every other finding, an error included, is reported and refuses nothing (`--documents` refuses as a search does, a previous proposals file excepted); for `--apply` also a malformed or unreadable proposals or decisions file, a proposals file outside the project, a plan that differs from the one `--expect-plan` names, a file changed while it ran, and a failed write, which is rolled back, except a file the rollback could not restore, which the error names. What this does not reach: a usage error — a missing KIND, or a KIND other than `allocation` and `trace` — exits 2 before the command runs.

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `KIND` | one of `allocation`, `trace` | required | 'allocation' (CARMA) or 'trace' (links) |
| `--config` | `FILE` | — | Path to the experiment's configuration file (YAML); without it the kind runs with its defaults |
| `--project` | `PATH` | — | Path to swcraft.yaml manifest (required) |
| `--format` | one of `text`, `json` | `text` | Output format: 'text' (default, the summary and the files written, or Apply's report) or 'json' (the result document the run writes, or Apply's report document, on stdout) |
| `--apply` | `FILE` | — | 'trace' only: apply the decisions in this proposals file (inside the project) -- write the accepted and confirmed links into the model, record the decisions in trace-decisions.yaml and mark them done in the file; all or nothing |
| `--dry-run` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | With --apply: print what Apply would write, and the plan's digest, and write nothing |
| `--expect-plan` | `DIGEST` | — | With --apply: refuse, writing nothing, when the plan differs from the one a dry run printed |
| `--report` | `PATH` | — | With --apply: also write the report to PATH after the run -- its Markdown form when PATH ends in .md, else what was printed (the JSON document with --format json, the text otherwise) |
| `--discard-pending` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | 'trace' search only: overwrite a previous proposals file that holds decisions not yet applied |
| `--documents` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | 'trace' only: print each document's requirements and links, the pass the configuration gives it and the proposals file a search would replace, and write nothing |
| `--labelling` | `JSON` | — | 'trace' search only: the documents labelled in this run, as JSON -- "all" or a list of document values -- in place of the configuration's search.labelling; recorded in the report, never written back |

## `swcraft guard` { #swcraft-guard }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft guard`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Answer an agent host's PreToolUse hook: read the tool call's JSON payload on stdin and answer in the host's form -- for Copilot, Codex and Claude Code the decision printed on stdout, exit 0; for Kiro a denial is exit 2 with one line on stderr and an allow exit 0 with nothing printed. For Copilot (the default), deny a known file tool's read or search that reaches the model directory or cannot be judged; for Codex (--host codex), also deny a patch or a shell command that reaches it; for Claude Code (--host claude), also deny an edit, a write or a shell command that reaches it, and every PowerShell call; for Kiro (--host kiro), judge Kiro's read, search, edit and shell tools alike and deny every tool it does not know; allow the rest (changes nothing)

This command is the model guard an agent host's hook runs: it reads one tool call as JSON on stdin and answers its host — under Copilot, Codex and Claude Code by printing its decision on stdout, `{}` to allow, and under Kiro as described below. With the default host (Copilot) it is the hook the project's hook file under `.github/hooks/` names; of the file and search tools it knows, it denies a read naming a path in the model root, and a search rooted at the model root, inside it or above it, its file pattern included; a call among them it cannot judge, such as arguments it cannot decode, a path it cannot resolve or a pattern that could climb with `..`, is denied too, as a read or search is when the guard itself fails unexpectedly. A saved Copilot answer in the system temporary directory stays allowed, and so is every other tool. The project is the `swcraft.yaml` in the call's working directory, and no other: without one it allows everything, and with one it cannot read it denies every file read and search but a saved answer. It changes nothing and exits 0 once it runs, a denial included, under every host but Kiro, whose denial is exit 2 (below); a project pinned to another SWCraft release is a warning and the decision stands. With `--host codex` it is the hook `.codex/hooks.json` names: it denies a patch naming a file in the model root, and a shell command with a word naming the model root or a path in it, a command it cannot parse, and an edit of a file the guards rest on — `swcraft.yaml`, `.mcp.json`, `.codex/`, `.claude/`, `.github/hooks/`, `.kiro/hooks/`, `.kiro/settings/` or `.kiro/agents/`, or of the `.github` or `.kiro` folder holding some of them; the project is the nearest folder upward holding both `swcraft.yaml` and `.codex/hooks.json`, and a deny carries its decision only inside `hookSpecificOutput`, the shape Codex reads. With `--host claude` it is the hook the project's `.claude/settings.json` names: it judges a read or search as for Copilot, denies an edit or write of a file in the model root, a shell command (`Bash` or `Monitor`) as under Codex, every PowerShell call, an edit of those same files, and a literal path into the review's own folder or naming a folder above it; the project is the nearest folder upward holding `swcraft.yaml` and `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json`, and also the folder `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` names when it holds them, each judged; a deny has the same `hookSpecificOutput` shape, the one Claude Code reads. With `--host kiro` it is the hook a file under the project's `.kiro/hooks/` names: it judges Kiro's file reads and listings as for Copilot, and its searches rooted at their include pattern, so a search over the whole project is denied; it denies an edit, write or delete of a file in the model root or of those same files, a shell command as under Codex, every PowerShell or cmd call, a code operation that changes files, a call whose arguments it does not know, and every tool it does not know, MCP tools excepted; the project is the nearest folder upward holding `swcraft.yaml` and `.kiro/hooks/`, from the call's working directory and from the hook's own, each judged, and a payload it cannot read is denied there. A deny is exit 2 with exactly one line on stderr, the reason, and nothing on stdout, the form Kiro reads; an allow prints nothing and exits 0. What this does not reach: a usage error exits 2 before the command runs; with the default host the terminal, file edits, a tool or path field outside its tables, and the other limits [The limits under Copilot](../model-guard.md#copilot-does-not-reach) lists; with `--host codex` a command that reaches the model without naming it, and the other limits of [The limits under Codex](../model-guard.md#codex-does-not-reach); with `--host kiro` the limits [What the guard under Kiro does not reach](../kiro.md#what-the-guard-under-kiro-does-not-reach) lists. A hook that cannot run at all — no `swcraft` on PATH, or one with no `guard` — makes Copilot deny every tool call in the project, SWCraft's own tools included, until this release's `swcraft` is on PATH. Under Codex a hook that cannot run is a failed hook, and Codex runs the tool anyway; an older `swcraft` invoked with `--host codex` rejects the option with a usage error, which Codex reads as a block of every shell command and edit. Claude Code does the same: with no `swcraft` it runs the tool, and an older one invoked with `--host claude` blocks every tool the hook names. Under Kiro a hook that cannot run, or that runs past its timeout, lets the tool run, and an older `swcraft` invoked with `--host kiro` exits 2 with its usage error, which Kiro reads as a block of its file and shell tools.

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `--host` | one of `copilot`, `codex`, `claude`, `kiro` | `copilot` | the host whose hook calls this: copilot (the default), codex, claude or kiro; codex, claude and kiro change the answer's shape and add the edit and shell rules; kiro alone denies with exit 2 and one stderr line instead of an answer on stdout |

## `swcraft change-report` { #swcraft-change-report }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft change-report`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Report what a change does to the architecture -- what changed, requirement links, the findings it introduced, resources, interface consumers, ARXML elements and the overviews before and after -- into &lt;dist_root>/change-report/ (git-diff-like revision arguments; writes nothing into the model)

This command writes `change-report.md`, `change-report-pr.md` (the same report without its pictures, for a pull request), `change-report.json` and the overview pictures under `<dist_root>/change-report/`, replacing the previous run's, and nothing into the model. It succeeds on a run that could read the project at both revisions, whatever the change introduced — a model with errors at either revision is reported, not refused. It fails, and writes nothing, on a project or a revision it could not read (an unknown revision, one that does not hold the model root, a model file that does not parse), a name declared twice at either revision, a report directory outside the project, over the model or on a file, and a project pinned to another SWCraft release. With `--fail-on` it fails after writing the report when the change introduced a finding of that level or above. What this does not reach: a usage error exits 2 before the command runs.

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `REV_A` | one value | — | Older revision (default: HEAD). If REV_B is omitted, compared against the working tree. |
| `REV_B` | one value | — | Newer revision. If omitted, the working tree is used. |
| `--project` | `PATH` | — | Path to swcraft.yaml manifest (required) |
| `--format` | one of `text`, `json` | `text` | Output format: 'text' (default, the path of the report written) or 'json' (the report's JSON document on stdout); the files are written either way |
| `--fail-on` | one of `never`, `warning`, `error` | `never` | Exit 1 after writing the report when the change introduces a finding of this level or above ('never', the default: the run succeeds whatever the change introduces) |
| `--no-diagrams` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | Leave the overview pictures out (drawing them needs Node.js) |

## `swcraft passport` { #swcraft-passport }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft passport`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Write the model's passport -- counts, distributions and lengths, with no name, no value and no text of the model -- as JSON to stdout or to --output, to send instead of a model that cannot be shared (writes nothing into the model)

This command writes the model's passport as JSON, to stdout or to the file `--output` names, and nothing into the model. The passport holds counts, distributions and lengths, and no name, no value and no text of the model. It succeeds on a run that could read the project and its model, whatever `check-model` would say of it: a model with errors still gets its passport. It fails, and writes no passport, on a project or a model file it could not read, a file `--output` names that it could not write, and a project pinned to another SWCraft release; its messages name no absolute path, and a model file it could not read is named by its layer and the kind of error alone, never by its name or its content, because they may travel with the passport. What this does not reach: which file it was, which `swcraft check-model` says; and a usage error exits 2 before the command runs.

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `--project` | `PATH` | — | Path to swcraft.yaml manifest (required) |
| `--output` | `FILE` | — | Write the passport to this file instead of stdout |

## `swcraft metrics` { #swcraft-metrics }

<!-- purpose: Running `swcraft metrics`: what it does, each option, and what it does when left out -->

Print the architecture metrics -- size, coupling, cohesion, coverage and integrity, each explained, and how they moved since a revision (read-only without --report; always exits 0 -- 'swcraft validate' is the gate)

Without `--report` this command writes no file. With it, it also writes `<dist_root>/metrics/metrics.md`, nothing into the model, and prints where. A report that cannot be written is a warning and moves no exit code; a project pinned to another SWCraft release gets its answer and a warning, and no file. It always succeeds on a run that could read the project — an empty or an uncomfortable answer is still an answer. A project it could not read is the failure it reports.

| Option or argument | Accepted values | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-h, --help` | nothing — the option is a switch | — | show this help message and exit |
| `--project` | `PATH` | — | Path to swcraft.yaml manifest (required) |
| `--since` | `REV`, repeatable | — | A revision to compare the working tree against, read as 'swcraft diff' reads one; repeat it for a series, the first named being the base. A revision that cannot be read fails the run |
| `--since-head` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | Compare against HEAD when it can be read; when it cannot, the report says why and the run still succeeds |
| `--format` | one of `text`, `json` | `text` | Output format: 'text' (default, the report with its explanations) or 'json' (versioned, machine-readable) |
| `--report` | nothing — the option is a switch | off | Also write the report as Markdown to &lt;dist_root>/metrics/metrics.md |

`--since` and `--since-head` cannot be given together.
